newsitem.title: USA: NHL-ROBITAILLE, GRETZKY BREAK DROUGHTS AS RANGERS BEAT CANADIENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-ROBITAILLE, GRETZKY BREAK DROUGHTS AS RANGERS BEAT CANADIENS.

text.p: Luc Robitaille and Wayne Gretzky broke five-game goal-scoring droughts and Mike Richter made 35 saves as the New York Rangers got their first home win in more than a month, 6-2 over the Montreal Canadiens Sunday.

Gretzky, Sergei Nemchinov and Brian Leetch each had a goal and an assist for the Rangers, who had been 0-3-1 at Madison Square Garden since October 27. New York (10-13-4) had a season-high 49 shots and is unbeaten in its last 10 home games against Montreal (seven wins, three ties).

"I think we played pretty solid tonight," said Rangers captain Mark Messier, who contributed two assists and has an eight-game points streak. "Winning and losing is such a fine line. I think doing the little things is most important."
He added: "We're still a below .500 team, but we're playing better in all areas."
Mark Recchi and Martin Rucinsky scored for the Canadiens, who have not won at New York since November 6, 1991.
"Tonight, we just collapsed," said Montreal coach Mario Tremblay. "We let them skate in the open ice."

Jeff Beukeboom's tally 16 seconds into the second period made it 2-1 and sparked a three-goal outburst. Robitaille then got his first goal since November 16 on a behind-the-back pass from Niklas Sundstrom after a Gretzky rebound.

"What's most important is the way I've been playing," Robitaille said. "I've been skating hard and finishing checks. It feels good (to score), but I honestly felt as good after the last two games as I do tonight."
Leetch, who has a 14-game points streak, capped the second-period scoring to make it 4-1.
Rucinsky, like Gretzky and Rucinsky, also scored for the first time since November 16 early in the third period. But Gretzky and Brian Noonan tallied 42 seconds apart midway through the period.
"Tonight was a really good team effort," Gretzky said. "We really concentrated on the little things."

In Detroit, Brian Skrudland's goal with 11:23 remaining broke a tie and the Florida Panthers scored on both of their shots in the third period to defeat the Red Wings 4-2, extending their unbeaten streak to six games.
Mark Fitzpatrick made 28 saves for Florida, which leads the league with 38 points and improved the NHL's top road record to 8-1-3.
Chris Osgood made only 14 saves and fell to 9-6-2. It took him 50 decisions to suffer six losses last season.
Sergei Fedorov and Nicklas Lidstrom tallied for the Red Wings. Detroit (14-9-3) did not suffer its ninth loss last season until January 8.
In Philadelphia, Scott Daniels' goal with just under eight minutes to play snapped a tie and lifted the Flyers to a 4-3 win over the Vancouver Canucks.
Ron Hextall needed just 16 saves for the Flyers, who are 2-0-1 in their last three home games.
Corey Hirsch stopped 28 shots for Vancouver, which has lost three of four on its six-game road trip.
Both teams combined for five goals in the third period to break open a 1-1 tie.
Vancouver captain Trevor Linden left after the second period with a left knee injury. He did not return and his status is unknown.
In St. Louis, Owen Nolan scored at even strength and on the power play in the first period and Bernie Nicholls added a goal and an assist as the San Jose Sharks beat the Blues 4-3.

Jeff Friesen also tallied for the Sharks, who are just 2-6-1 in their last nine games. Chris Terreri made 31 saves for his third victory of the season and first since October 20, also against St Louis.
Geoff Courtnall, Stephane Matteau and Peter Zezel had goals for the Blues, who have alternated wins and losses in their last five contests following a five-game winning streak.
In Anaheim, Kevin Todd's goal snapped a tie with 2:51 remaining and Paul Kariya scored twice to help the Mighty Ducks defeat the Edmonton Oilers 4-2.

The Oilers pulled goalie Curtis Joseph for an extra attacker with 75 seconds left, but Kariya scored into an empty net 15 seconds later to seal the victory. Kariya has five goals and four assists during a six-game points streak.
Joe Sacco also scored and Teemu Selanne had two assists for the Ducks, who have won four of their last five games. Guy Hebert madee 24 saves and has allowed just eight goals in his last six games.
Mariusz Czerkawski and Todd Marchant tallied for the Oilers, who lost for the second time in seven games (4-2-1).
